targets.claim: The author was elected to the Kentucky State Senate in 1967 and became the first woman and first person of color to serve in the body.
Rand Paul declared he is running for president of the United States.

The author finds it 'almost unfathomable' that a politician from her own state is attempting to launch his presidential campaign on a record that includes questioning landmark voting rights and civil rights legislation.
Paul's campaign team told reporters his campaign announcement message would be about 'expanding the Republican Party' — a message of inclusion.
The author criticized Paul's campaign team's message of inclusion as hype.
Paul has questioned the Civil Rights Act and claimed that private business owners have a right to discriminate.
Paul thinks the Department of Education 'should be done away with.'
Paul seeks to limit women's choices/rights in Washington.
Paul currently opposes protections for DREAMers from deportation.
When asked about the need for a more robust Voting Rights Act following the Supreme Court's dismantling of the law, Paul dismissively remarked, 'We have an African-American President.'
The author urged the GOP to have a real commitment to the issues facing minority communities.
